notices.html: Von Thun Farms' Fall Festival opens this Saturday, September 19: a Dogs and Dinos corn maze, hayrides, duck races and pumpkin picking, $17.99 per person, with one free grandparent this opening weekend.
Terhune Orchards' Fall Family Fun Weekends need timed tickets: book online for $19.95 per person to beat the $24.95 door price.
Battleview Orchards' pumpkin season start date isn't confirmed yet: apple, peach and cherry picking are already out for the year after the spring freeze, so call before heading over.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend: Fall Family Fun Weekends continues Saturdays and Sundays through November 1, 10am to 5pm, with the corn and hay maze, pony rides, pumpkin picking and live music. Apple and peach picking are out for the season this year after the spring freeze, so it's veggies and flowers instead, and tickets run $19.95 per person in advance online or $24.95 at the door. Call 609-924-2310 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: apples are ready to pick, Cortland, Empire, Fuji, Gala, Golden Delicious, Jonagold, Red Delicious and Stayman, plus tomatoes are still coming in. This is a simple, no-frills PYO farm with no festival extras, and the fields close for entry at 5:15pm. Call 609-448-0629 to confirm before you head over.
blurbs.vonthun: This weekend: the Fall Festival opens for the season on Saturday, with a Dogs and Dinos corn maze, hayrides, pedal karts, duck races and a pumpkin patch, running Saturdays and Sundays 10am to 5pm through November 8. Apples are ready in 8 varieties, blackberry season has ended, and admission is $17.99 per person with one free grandparent per paid admission this opening weekend. Call 732-329-8656 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: no change from last week, the corn maze and pumpkins don't open until September 26, and u-pick blueberry season is long over, though fresh and frozen berries are still sold in the farm market. Call 609-758-8514 to confirm before making a special trip.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: still no pick-your-own tree fruit after the spring freeze wiped out apples, cherries, peaches and nectarines, though a sunflower field is open for cutting your own this month. Pumpkin picking and hayrides may start around September 19, but that date isn't firmly confirmed yet, so call 732-462-0756 before you go.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: apples and pumpkins are in full swing as part of the Fall Harvest Festival, running through October 31 with hayrides, a corn maze, gem mining and duck races. Pricing seems to vary between hayride-only tickets and full admission, so call the Pick Your Own Hotline 609-654-5894 to confirm the current price before you go.
blurbs.dinosafari: This weekend: still closed for the season, since it only ran July 1 through August 16. It's expected to return next summer, so there's no need for a special trip until then.
